Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
442 AM EDT Thu Apr 30 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
The probability of mainly light rain has increased late
Saturday into Saturday night.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Lingering showers across Long Island and S CT early this
morning, followed by a cold front passage this 
afternoon/evening isolated to widely scattered showers. 

2) Some light rain is possible late Saturday into Saturday
night despite low pressure likely passing well offshore. 

3) A warming trend early next week may be accompanied by
unsettled conditions next Tuesday or Wednesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Widespread showers have ended from the NYC metro north and west.
Showers will continue early this morning across mainly eastern
Long Island and southeastern CT, but should diminish and push
east through mid morning. Additional rainfall will be light and
generally just a few tenths at most. 

The actual cold front will move across the area this afternoon.
Isolated to widely scattered showers may develop with the 
front. Additional rainfall with these showers will be mainly 
light. 

The cold front pushes offshore late afternoon into this evening
with dry conditions prevailing through Friday afternoon.


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
Closed mid level low will persist over southeast Canada Friday
night through early Sunday with troughing over the eastern US. 
Several shortwaves will rotate around the upper low during this 
period, with one passing across the area Friday night. This wave
may develop a few showers Friday night.

Another more amplified shortwave rounds the base of the trough
over the southeast and Middle Atlantic on Saturday. This will 
develop low pressure off the NC/VA coast Saturday before 
tracking ENE as it gradually strengthens. The model guidance 
has trended slightly further NW over the last 24 hours. Despite 
this trend, the center of the low is still progged to pass 
250-300 miles SE of the Long Island coast Saturday night. PoPs 
have increased across the area with a chance of mainly light 
rain late Saturday into Saturday night. Some of this rain may be
attributed to lift in advance of the approaching mid to upper 
trough axis and divergence aloft from the associated upper jet. 

Significant rain, wind, and coastal impacts are not expected
with this system. The latest rainfall forecast ranges from a 
few hundredths inland to potentially a few tenths across the 
east end.


.KEY MESSAGE 3...
Cool conditions this weekend will trend warmer early next
week. Highs struggling to get out of the 50s Saturday and 
Sunday should warm into the 60s on Monday and then potentially 
the 70s away from the immediate coast on Tuesday. 

Another frontal system may approach the area Tuesday into next 
Wednesday bringing the next chance of showers. The best chance
of showers is still uncertain as it will revolve around the 
timing and amplification of the next mid-upper level trough.

&&

.AVIATION /09Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
MVFR to IFR this morning with local LIFR conditions. After cold
fropa on today, conditions should improve from west to east 
during the afternoon, with a return to VFR late this afternoon 
into early this evening (21Z-23Z). However, the return to VFR 
may be off by +/- 1 to 3 hours. 

S to SE flow shifts to the W to NW by mid-morning. Winds should 
remain at around 10 kt or less.

Steady rain showers have ended for the metro terminals and
Lower Hudson Valley terminals. Rain showers continue for eastern
terminals, but will come to an end from west to east, with an
end time for KGON by 10Z. 

NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Amendments likely due to changes in flight categories.

Return to VFR for metro terminals is 21-23z, +/- 1 to 3 hours. 

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY...

Thursday night: VFR. NW winds G15-20kt possible at the NYC metros 
mainly in the evening. 

Friday: VFR with NW flow 10-20 kt.

Saturday: Chance of light rain with MVFR cond mainly E of the NYC 
metros late in the afternoon and at night. 

Sunday and Monday: VFR. 

Tuesday: Mainly VFR. MVFR or lower in any showers. Highest
chances for showers and MVFR or lower conditions across Lower
Hudson Valley.

Wednesday: Mainly VFR in the morning. MVFR or lower in any
showers. Chances for showers increase from the morning to the
afternoon.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
E swells will around 5 ft on the ocean waters through this 
afternoon. No changes were made to the SCA in effect for the 
ocean waters out 20 nm. Swells should start subsiding tonight 
along with increasing NW flow. This will allow wave heights to
settle below 5 ft through Friday. Wind gusts are expected to 
remain below 25 kt.

Low pressure is expected to pass well offshore Saturday night.
There is a low chance for seas to build closer to 5 ft and 
winds gusting closer to 25 kt, especially east of Moriches 
Inlet, if the low were to track a bit closer to our waters. 
Confidence is low in this scenario with a higher chance 
conditions remain below SCA levels through the weekend. 

The pressure gradient tightens and winds increase on Monday. SCA 
conditions are possible Monday into Tuesday.

&&
